American voters have given the Democratic Party control of both the House and the Senate, placing their faith in candidates representing a broad range of backgrounds and ideas. Rep. Jason Crow, who won reelection in Colorado’s 6th District, helped lead the selection process for Democratic candidates in blue, red, and swing states. How will these very diverse new lawmakers coalesce under one tent? And how will they go about crafting a new foreign policy that will resonate with the middle class?
Crow, a former Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, will join FP’s Ravi Agrawal for a discussion about the Democrats’ vision and what areas of President Donald Trump’s policies they might challenge in Congress.

Host and Guests

Jason Crow

U.S. representative, D-CO

Jason Crow represents Colorado’s 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives. A former Army Ranger, he served three tours in Iraq and Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division and 75th Ranger Regiment, earning the Bronze Star for his leadership. He now serves on the House Armed Services and Intelligence committees.

What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy

November 5, 2026

Results are in, and Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 U.S. midterms. And with voters focused on the cost of living, foreign policy was an unusually impactful driver at the ballot box: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring. How might Democrats use their new power over spending and oversight to challenge Trump’s agenda in his final two years in office? How will allies and adversaries read the results? Susan Glasser, a staff writer at the New Yorker and former editor in chief of Foreign Policy, joined FP Live to break down what the midterms mean for congressional power and for America’s standing in the world.

After Israel Votes

October 29, 2026

On Oct. 27, Israelis voted in their first national election since the Hamas attacks of Oct. 7, 2023. The vote was widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Whether he or his more centrist competitor Gadi Eisenkot manage to form a government will determine not only the future of Israeli democracy but also its approach to Gaza and the West Bank, its relationship with the United States, and its standing abroad. Dahlia Scheindlin is one of Israel’s leading political analysts and pollsters. As coalition bargaining unfolds, she joined FP Live to break down the political scenarios, what they mean for Israeli democracy, and how they could reshape Israel’s foreign policy.

Where Ukraine Goes From Here

October 21, 2026

U.S. President Donald Trump’s so-called energy cease-fire hasn’t stopped Russia from bombing Ukrainian electricity and oil infrastructure. Nor has it stopped Ukraine from attacking Russian refineries. With winter approaching, Kyiv is racing to shore up its defenses and continue targeting Russia’s wartime economy—even as the United States begins to purchase Russian diesel. How should Kyiv’s strategy evolve? And how do the growing connections between Russia, Iran, China, and North Korea complicate matters? Andrea Kendall-Taylor is a former CIA analyst and expert on Russia and Eurasia at the Center for a New American Security. She joined FP’s Ravi Agrawal for a look at Ukraine’s diplomatic and battlefield options.

Why Spain Is Standing Up to Trump

October 14, 2026

Many countries have incorporated flattering U.S. President Donald Trump into their strategies for managing relations with the White House. Not Spain. Under Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Madrid has clashed with the Trump administration on Iran, Israel, Venezuela, and funding NATO. Trump, for his part, has called Spain a “terrible partner” and threatened to cut off trade. Is Spain’s strategy working? Voters may decide for themselves, with a snap election called for Nov. 29. 
José Manuel Albares, Spain’s foreign minister and a longtime advisor to Sánchez, joined FP Live to discuss his country’s foreign policy.
